rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction protections and relocation payments
rules.requirement: A landlord can evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only if one of the 17 just cause reasons in Section 37.9(a) is the dominant motive; a lease expiring or a change of ownership is not just cause, and just cause is also needed to remove housing services like parking, storage or laundry. For no-fault evictions (owner/relative move-in, demolition or removal, temporary capital improvement work, substantial rehabilitation) and Ellis Act evictions, the landlord must pay relocation money set each March 1.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes. Relocation for notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27: owner/relative move-in, demolition/removal, capital improvement, substantial rehab: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, +$5,497 per tenant 60+ or disabled or household with minor children. Ellis Act: $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, +$7,443.90 per tenant 62+ or disabled.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. The eviction protections also reach some tenancies exempt from rent increase limits, including newly built units first certified for occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies where Costa-Hawkins allows rent increases, and some units whose rent is regulated by another government agency. Relocation amounts depend on the date the notice is served and adjust every March 1.
rules.exemptions: The sources do not list units fully exempt from the eviction rules. Soft-story seismic retrofit work allows temporary removal of some housing services if the landlord follows Section 37.2(r). Relocation for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days is governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 instead of § 37.9C.
rules.penalty: Unlawful eviction or attempted eviction may subject the landlord to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.reason: All five candidates describe provisions of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance (Admin. Code ch. 37): the § 37.9 just cause requirement and the § 37.9A/37.9C relocation payments, so they were merged into one record. The 2026-03-01 date is an annual relocation adjustment and is not used as the effective date.
